why: All three challenge steps confirm the finding. (1) The quote exists VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md` line 86, inside a <Note> block in the "Pipe data through Claude" section, reads in full: "As of Claude Code v2.1.128, piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status. To work with larger inputs, write the content to a file and reference the file path in your prompt instead of piping it." The claimed quote is the first two sentences character-for-character; the unquoted third sentence is a workaround suggestion and does not reverse the conclusion. (2) The cited code says what was claimed. apps/cli/src/index.ts:423-442 `readPrompt` — it enters the stdin branch when `--stdin` is present or (no positional message and `process.stdin.isTTY` is false), then does `const chunks: string[] = []; const reader = Bun.stdin.stream().getReader()` and loops `while (true) { const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if (done) break; chunks.push(decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })) }` before `chunks.join('')`. There is no running byte counter, no length comparison, no throw, no `process.exit`. (3) Nothing one layer up or down supplies the cap. Layer up: the only two callers are `cmdSend` (:576) and `cmdRun` (:766) — `cmdRun` is this fork's `claude -p` analogue, spawning a local headless server in printMode — and both validate only `!message.trim()`; a binary-safe `grep -ran` over apps/cli/src finds `Bun.stdin`/`process.stdin` at exactly two lines (:427, :430), so there is no second stdin reader (no stream-json input path) that might cap. Layer down: the message travels the WsRpcServer (packages/server-core/src/transport/server.ts), which constructs `new WebSocketServer({ server })` (:294, :310) with no `maxPayload` option — a repo-wide `grep -ran maxPayload` over packages/server-core/src, packages/server/src and apps/cli/src returns zero hits — so the `ws` default is 100 MiB, well above 10 MB, and even that would surface as a connection close, not a clear error. No RPC handler enforces a text-message size limit (the only "too large" errors in packages/server-core/src/handlers are image-attachment resizes in files.ts:324-336). The nearest same-named constants are in a SIBLING subsystem and do NOT apply: `ProcessSupervisor.MAX_STDIN_DATA_BYTES = 1 MiB` and `MAX_STDIN_WRITE_BYTES = 64 KiB` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:25-27) bound what the host writes to a CHILD process's stdin, not what the CLI reads from its own. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) — none concerns stdin or the CLI. Not a de-brand, gateway or dropped-subscription product difference either: docs/cli.md:118-125 and :195-199 actively document piping stdin into both `nessy-general-agent send` and `nessy-general-agent run`, so the fork ships the surface the doc caps and simply never caps it.
correctedState: Confirmed as stated, with the scope made precise. `readPrompt` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:423-442) reads piped stdin unbounded: lines 429-438 push every decoded chunk into a `string[]` and join it, with no byte accounting and no ceiling, so a 10 MB+ pipe is accepted silently and simply consumes memory (roughly twice the input, since chunks are held before the join). Both entry points are affected — `cmdSend` (:576) and `cmdRun` (:766), the latter being this fork's headless `claude -p` analogue — and each validates only that the result is non-empty (`!message.trim()`). No layer supplies the missing cap: apps/cli has exactly one stdin reader; the WsRpcServer sets no `maxPayload` (packages/server-core/src/transport/server.ts:294, :310), leaving the `ws` 100 MiB default, which is ten times the documented limit and would manifest as a connection close rather than the documented clear error; and no RPC handler length-checks the message text. The 1 MiB / 64 KiB stdin constants in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:25-27 belong to the child-process supervisor and bound host-to-child writes, not CLI stdin intake. Two incidental observations outside the claim: the decoder is used with `{ stream: true }` and never flushed with a final `decoder.decode()`, so a trailing incomplete multibyte sequence is dropped; and docs/cli.md documents stdin piping for `send` and `run` without mentioning any size limit, so the fork's own documentation would need the same line if a cap is added.
